title: SHE IS MORE RIGHTEOUS THAN I

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "As she was being brought out, she sent a message to her father-in-law. 'I am pregnant by the man who owns these,' she said. And she added, 'See if you recognize whose seal and cord and staff these are.' Judah recognized them and said, 'She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn't give her to my son Shelah.' And he did not sleep with her again." - Gen 38:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Tamar is led out to be executed, she quietly sends Judah his own seal, cord, and staff with a simple message: "I am pregnant by the man who owns these. See if you recognize them." In an instant, everything changes. Judah recognizes his own belongings, and the truth crashes down on him. He is the father. He is the guilty one.

And here, at last, we see something good in Judah. He does not scramble to cover it up or twist his way out. He confesses openly: "She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn't give her to my son Shelah." He admits that his own wrong — breaking his promise and denying Tamar her rightful future — was the root of it all. This honest confession is a turning point in Judah's life. From here, he begins to become a changed man.

There is real hope in this moment. Judah could have doubled down, destroyed the evidence, and let Tamar die to protect himself. Instead, when confronted, he owned his sin. That is what genuine repentance looks like — not excuses, not blame-shifting, but honest confession: "I was wrong."

When you are confronted with your own sin, which path will you take? The hard, humbling road of "I was wrong" is the road to grace and change. God resists the proud who cover up, but "gives grace to the humble" who own their sin (Jas 4:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When confronted with my sin, do I confess or cover up?
2. Can I honestly say "I was wrong" rather than shift the blame?
3. Where is God calling me to humble, honest repentance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I am confronted with my sin, give me the humility to say "I was wrong" rather than to cover up or blame. Thank You that You give grace to the humble. Change me as You changed Judah. Amen.
